mission: Ben talks to Kael about Veraine's message. Kael doesn't share its contents but acknowledges the parallel — same wound, different response. The institutional lie subplot deepens as Ben sees how the Jedi and Sith both used Kael.
why_now: Kael walked out — Ben goes after him. The Kael/Veraine parallel needs its first explicit acknowledgment.
conflict: Kael doesn't want to discuss the message but is honest about the parallel when pressed — both he and Veraine were conscripted, captured, and used as infrastructure. The only difference is that she broke out and he didn't.
turning_point: Ben says something that surprises Kael — acknowledges that the Jedi using Sith captives as seal infrastructure was wrong, not just tactically questionable but morally indefensible. Kael isn't used to Jedi conceding points.
opening_hook: Kael is sitting outside the outpost, staring at stars he doesn't recognize. A thousand years changes constellations.
closing_hook: Kael, after a long silence: 'She'll come for me. At some point. She'll try to recruit me.' Beat. 'She might have a point.' He doesn't say which point.
emotional_trajectory: Careful approach -> honest vulnerability (both characters) -> ambiguous warning

stakes.personal: Ben treating Kael as a person — breaking the institutional pattern
stakes.interpersonal: First real trust between Ben and Kael
stakes.external: Kael's vulnerability to Veraine's pitch is a real strategic risk

setting: Outside the Brotherhood Outpost — night sky, alien stars, thin place ambience
sensory_details: Unfamiliar constellations; cold air; the outpost's dark-side ambience muted by distance; Kael's Force presence — guarded but not hostile, more open than Ben has felt it
action_beats: Ben finds Kael on the outpost's exterior steps, face tilted toward constellations that shifted while he slept a thousand years
Ben sits down on the cold stone beside Kael, leaving a deliberate arm's length of space
Kael turns Veraine's data tablet over in his hands before pocketing it without showing Ben the message
notes: Kael's arc: lie_questioned (first touch) — Ben treating him as a person, not a tool, challenges his assumption that conviction is always a trap. But it's early; the questioning is tentative.
